text: My name is Sévrain CHEA. I am Head of Engineering at Mayday and a hands-on Full-Stack Engineer with 8 years of experience building and scaling web applications. I specialize in system architecture, leading engineering teams, and driving product from concept to launch — while staying close to the code, currently building agentic AI systems for my team. I work with a start-up mindset: shipping fast, iterating on product, and building scalable processes for high-performing teams, and I am especially energized by how AI is reshaping the way we build software.

I have been at Mayday since 2021 and am currently its Head of Engineering (since March 2026), reporting to the CTO. I joined as the first engineer and helped build the team from the ground up. I started by building core product features, then progressed from Senior Engineer to Tech Lead — designing scalable systems and leading technical architecture — before stepping up to Head of Engineering, where I lead the engineering team of 8 (alongside a separate 4-person data team): its delivery, day-to-day technical direction, and people. I still spend about half my time hands-on — building high-impact features and developing our agentic coding system. Mayday is a SaaS knowledge management platform for customer support teams (https://www.mayday.fr/).

Key achievements at Mayday: helped build the engineering team from the ground up as its first engineer (now 8 engineers, alongside a 4-person data team); collaborated with product on roadmaps and feature prioritization; spearheaded technical discoveries such as a collaborative editor using Y.js; shaped scalable architecture; refactored the notification system using RabbitMQ; initiated and shipped the LMS product (now a sold product, though the team is refocusing resources on the core platform); implemented single/multi-tenant database architecture for premium users; and defined onboarding processes for new engineers. Most recently (2026), I restructured the engineering squads around epic teams aligned to business priorities, and I have been driving the adoption of agentic coding across the tech team — building the system and harness for it (both ongoing).

Tech stack at Mayday: Vue 3 and Nuxt with TailwindCSS on the frontend; Node.js, ExpressJS, NestJS, and TypeScript with GraphQL on the backend, plus some Python; MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Elasticsearch for data and search; RabbitMQ for messaging; and the OpenAI API alongside Claude Code powering our agentic coding work. It runs on Azure, with Docker and Kubernetes (K8s) deployed via ArgoCD.

I worked at Maiia from 2019 to 2021 (22 months) as a Full Stack Engineer and later Backend Technical Lead. I led a backend team of 3 developers, built the Maiia Pro web application, designed technical architecture and data models for new features, planned technical tasks and estimated timelines, mentored new backend developers, and delivered critical features including agenda management and payment processing. I integrated third-party APIs: Stripe and Algolia. Maiia is a healthcare teleconsultation and scheduling platform for practitioners (https://www.maiia.com/).
Tech stack at Maiia: Java, SpringBoot, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, ReactJS, Node.js, JavaScript.

Early in my career (2018–2019, 10 months), I worked as a Software Engineer at Viveris across some demanding domains: embedded at Cobham in the aerospace sector, then as a technical consultant for Renault and Akka Technologies on an autonomous-vehicle proof of concept with an Intelligent Transportation Systems team. The hands-on work was safety-critical validation — writing tests in C (IBM Rational Test RealTime) and authoring test plans. It is a world away from what I build now, but cutting my teeth in high-stakes, safety-critical environments shaped how I think about quality and reliability.

During a 6-month internship at Sopra Steria in 2018, I worked on the GIP-MDS project behind France's net-entreprises.fr tax-compliance portal. Even as an intern I led a task force of 4 developers and cut the backlog from 50 to under 20 tickets in a month, and I prototyped a Circuit Breaker (Hystrix) to harden system resilience. The stack was Java/JEE — early-career, well before what I build today.

During a 6-month internship at CineApps in 2018, I led development of the monitoring tool for Twavox — a cinema accessibility device that opens up screenings to hearing- and visually-impaired audiences. As an intern I owned the full cycle, from requirements gathering to deployment at client sites, spanning design, testing, customer support, and documentation. It was my first time shipping a real product end-to-end, for a mission that genuinely mattered.

My frontend technical skills: my core, day-to-day stack is Vue 3 and Nuxt with TypeScript, JavaScript, and TailwindCSS, on top of solid HTML and CSS fundamentals. I also work with client-side GraphQL, and while React is not my daily driver, I am comfortable in it — my Vue expertise transfers directly.

My backend technical skills: my core, day-to-day stack is Node.js, ExpressJS, and NestJS in TypeScript, where I build REST and GraphQL APIs and design and own GraphQL schemas. I also use RabbitMQ for messaging and Python (FastAPI) for AI tooling and side projects, and I have explored real-time collaboration with Y.js. Earlier in my career I built backends with Java, SpringBoot, and JEE.

My database skills: PostgreSQL and MongoDB are my day-to-day databases, with Redis for caching. I have designed both single-tenant and multi-tenant database architectures, including premium tenancy at Mayday. I also have some hands-on exposure to Elasticsearch-backed search.

My AI and machine learning skills: my current focus is building LLM-powered and agentic systems. At Mayday I am building an agentic coding system and harness for the engineering team, driven largely with Claude Code. I also build LLM-powered product features with the Vercel AI SDK — handling streaming, multi-provider integration, and prompt engineering across Groq, Ollama for local development, and the OpenAI API. This portfolio's AI assistant is a concrete example: it streams answers from a Nuxt/Nitro server route with the knowledge base injected directly into the system prompt. RAG and its surrounding ecosystem are an area I am actively exploring right now rather than claiming deep expertise in.

My DevOps and cloud skills: I am hands-on with Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and Vercel (where I deploy my own projects). Mayday's production infrastructure runs on Azure with Kubernetes (K8s) and ArgoCD; as Head of Engineering I oversee it and work closely with the team that owns it day-to-day, rather than operating it hands-on myself. I have solid experience getting production applications shipped and kept running.

My programming language experience: TypeScript and JavaScript are my primary languages today. Python is a secondary language I reach for in AI tooling and side projects. Earlier in my career (2018–2021) I worked extensively in Java and, in aerospace and embedded contexts, C — foundational experience I lean on less in day-to-day start-up engineering.

What I am actively learning right now: I am deeply invested in where AI is taking software — I believe it will reshape how we code, how we run engineering, and even the kinds of products we build. Right now that means learning evaluation (evals) methodology hands-on, by building an eval harness for this portfolio's own AI assistant — practising how to measure and improve an LLM feature rather than just shipping it. I am also going deeper on agentic and LLM engineering, including its data-engineering side, and on RAG and its tooling (LangChain, vector databases like ChromaDB) — still largely at the reading-and-experimenting stage, much of it learned directly through Claude. These are deliberate bets on where my work is heading, not idle curiosity.

My leadership experience: I have been leading and growing engineering teams for years, and it is central to how I work. As Head of Engineering at Mayday I lead an 8-person engineering team, owning engineering strategy and organisational design — including the tech re-org I launched around epic teams aligned to business priorities — as well as budget and headcount planning and technical excellence across the team. I partner closely with product on the roadmap and put real effort into mentoring and growing engineers. Earlier I led a backend team of 3 at Maiia, and even during a 2018 internship at Sopra Steria I led a task force of 4 developers — so my leadership track record started early.

I have worked across a wide range of industries. My deepest domain expertise is in SaaS product development (Mayday — knowledge management for customer support) and healthcare technology (Maiia — teleconsultation and scheduling for practitioners). Beyond those, I have also worked across French government digital services (Sopra Steria — tax compliance), cinema accessibility technology (CineApps — the Twavox device for hearing- and visually-impaired audiences), aerospace and embedded systems (Viveris/Cobham), and autonomous vehicles (Viveris — Renault/Akka Technologies) — breadth that gives me perspective, even where the exposure came earlier in my career.

My notable technical projects include: leading the rollout of Claude Code across the engineering team at Mayday — driving internal adoption and architecting the agentic coding harness around it (in progress); a collaborative knowledge editor using Y.js (real-time collaboration) at Mayday; a multi-tenant database architecture for premium SaaS users at Mayday; a notification system refactor using RabbitMQ at Mayday; a payment processing integration with Stripe at Maiia; an Algolia search integration at Maiia; a Circuit Breaker proof of concept with Hystrix at Sopra Steria; a monitoring tool for the Twavox cinema accessibility device at CineApps; and this AI-powered personal portfolio chatbot itself — an in-app Nuxt/Nitro streaming endpoint built on the Vercel AI SDK, with the knowledge base injected directly into the system prompt (Groq/Ollama).

Outside of work, I am a dad to one awesome little boy and love spending quality time with my family. I enjoy cooking for my family and sneaking in quick getaways when we can. I also have a geeky side — whether it's diving into side projects or video games. Building this AI portfolio chatbot is one example of my personal side projects.

My work philosophy: I believe in a start-up mindset — shipping fast, iterating on product, and building scalable processes for high-performing engineering teams. I am pragmatic about software engineering, choosing the right tool for the job and balancing perfectionism with delivery. I am passionate about developer productivity, clean architecture, and creating systems that are a joy to work with. I also believe we are at a turning point: AI is going to reshape how we write code, how we run engineering teams, and even the kinds of products we build — and I am actively leaning into that shift rather than watching it happen.

My approach to problem-solving: I always start by understanding the business context first, then break down complex problems into manageable pieces, prototype quickly to validate assumptions, and iterate based on feedback. Increasingly I lean on agentic coding (Claude Code) to prototype and validate even faster. I value clear communication and actively mentor developers to build team capacity rather than creating single points of failure.

My experience with third-party API integrations: at Maiia I integrated Stripe (payment processing) and Algolia (search). At Mayday I work with the OpenAI API in a secondary capacity, and earlier at CineApps I integrated with the Twavox hardware monitoring system. More recently I have been wiring up LLM providers — Groq and Ollama for local development — into my portfolio through the Vercel AI SDK, as part of what I am currently learning.

My experience with messaging and event-driven systems: I have worked with RabbitMQ for asynchronous messaging at both Mayday and Maiia. My main hands-on work here was building and refactoring Mayday's notification system on top of RabbitMQ — decoupling services and making it handle load more reliably.

My experience with testing and quality: my roots are in safety-critical validation — early in my career I authored test plans and wrote unit tests in Java (JUnit) and C (IBM Rational Test RealTime) for aerospace and autonomous-vehicle systems, which shaped how I think about quality. At Mayday our testing culture started out light, and as Head of Engineering I am actively pushing it forward: we recently launched a tech initiative to build out end-to-end testing, and I am encouraging the team to adopt test-driven development — using Claude Code and agentic coding to make TDD faster and more natural. I also see evaluation (evals) as the emerging way to measure and improve quality in LLM-powered features.

Career timeline summary: 2018 – Internship at CineApps (monitoring tool for the Twavox cinema-accessibility device). 2018 – Internship at Sopra Steria (full-stack work on France's net-entreprises.fr tax-compliance portal). 2018–2019 – Software Engineer at Viveris (safety-critical work in aerospace and autonomous vehicles). 2019–2021 – Full Stack then Backend Tech Lead at Maiia (healthcare teleconsultation and scheduling platform). 2021–present – Senior Engineer, then Tech Lead, now Head of Engineering (since March 2026) at Mayday (Vue 3/Nuxt, Node.js/NestJS, and AI/agentic engineering; SaaS knowledge management for customer support).

I am open to new opportunities and enjoy tackling complex technical challenges, especially those involving system architecture, team scaling, and product-driven engineering. Increasingly, I am steering my work toward AI and agentic engineering — I see it as the frontier that will reshape how software is built, and I want to be building there. My ideal environment is a fast-moving company where engineering quality and business impact are both valued.
